sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即便是在那个黑胶唱片盛行的年代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满美感的、拥有50年历史的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For months, a Hollywood drama has been unfolding that's fit for the big screen.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，好莱坞上演了一出足以搬上大银幕的戏剧。

sentences.en: It's a corporate love triangle with a cast of characters including a billionaire scion, a tech giant, and the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是一场企业三角恋，角色阵容包括亿万富翁的后代、科技巨头以及美国总统。

sentences.en: Now that story appears to be coming to a close, but with a twist ending.
sentences.zh: 现在这个故事似乎要画上句号了，但结局却出人意料。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Nicole Sperling, Lauren Hirsch, and Jonathan Mahler explain why the merger between Paramount and Warner Brothers has left Hollywood in a state of shock,
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事妮可·斯珀林、劳伦·赫什和乔纳森·马勒将解释为什么派拉蒙与华纳兄弟的合并让好莱坞陷入了震惊，

sentences.en: and why the deal could reshape our political and cultural landscape.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么这笔交易可能会重塑我们的政治和文化格局。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月4日，星期三。

sentences.en: Lauren, Nicole, Jonathan, good to have you here.
sentences.zh: 劳伦、妮可、乔纳森，很高兴你们能来。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来。

sentences.en: So we have gathered the three of you here today because for months now, there has been this looming question over Hollywood about who was going to buy Warner Brothers.
sentences.zh: 今天把三位请来，是因为几个月来，好莱坞一直悬而未决的问题就是：谁会收购华纳兄弟？

sentences.en: And we finally seem to have our answer.
sentences.zh: 现在我们终于有了答案。

sentences.en: It's going to be Paramount with the winning bid.
sentences.zh: 最终胜出的竞标者是派拉蒙。

sentences.en: Lauren, you've covered every inch of this corporate dealmaking so far.
sentences.zh: 劳伦，到目前为止，你报道了这笔企业交易的每一个细节。

sentences.en: Nicole, you have been paying close attention to how Hollywood is reacting to all of this.
sentences.zh: 妮可，你一直密切关注着好莱坞对此事的反应。

sentences.en: And Jonathan, your extensive reporting on the Murdochs means that you are pretty well positioned to comment on what it means when billionaires come to town.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，你对默多克家族的深入报道，让你非常有资格评论亿万富翁进军好莱坞意味着什么。

sentences.en: So Jonathan, I want to start with you.
sentences.zh: 那么乔纳森，我想先从你开始。

sentences.en: Can you explain why this deal matters?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这笔交易为何如此重要吗？

sentences.en: I mean, on the most basic level, this deal matters a ton because we are talking about the creation of an enormous media empire here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从最基本的层面来看，这笔交易意义重大，因为我们谈论的是一个庞大媒体帝国的诞生。

sentences.en: We're talking about Under One Single Roof, Paramount, CBS, HBO, Warner Brothers, CNN, Nickelodeon, MTV, and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是将派拉蒙、CBS、HBO、华纳兄弟、CNN、尼克儿童频道、MTV等等，全部整合在同一个屋檐下。

sentences.en: We are talking about a huge media company.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一家巨型媒体公司。

sentences.en: And we're also talking about Larry and David Ellison, who are, you know, new media power brokers.
sentences.zh: 我们还要谈谈拉里·埃里森和戴维·埃里森，他们是新晋的媒体权力掮客。

sentences.en: Larry, of course, was the founder of Oracle in the 70s, an original kind of legacy software company.
sentences.zh: 拉里当然是70年代甲骨文公司的创始人，那是一家老牌软件公司。

sentences.en: You know, a billionaire many, many times over who has, in recent years, gotten very close to the president, to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他是一位身家极高的亿万富翁，近年来与总统唐纳德·特朗普走得很近。

sentences.en: And his son, David, who was at one point an aspiring actor who then went on to become a film producer and financier and then bought Paramount.
sentences.zh: 而他的儿子戴维，曾一度梦想成为演员，后来转型为电影制片人和投资人，并收购了派拉蒙。

sentences.en: And now with his new deal, Warner Brothers Discovery, he's going to become one of the most powerful media moguls in the world almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着这笔收购华纳兄弟探索频道的交易，他几乎一夜之间成为了世界上最有权势的媒体大亨之一。

sentences.en: And so the two of them together are now emerging as a new kind of father-son duo, really, you would have to say, kind of outstripping the influence of Rupert and Lachlan Murdoch.
sentences.zh: 所以他们父子俩现在正作为一种新型的父子组合崛起，不得不说，他们的影响力甚至超过了鲁珀特·默多克和拉克兰·默多克。

sentences.en: They are the new Murdochs, but quite possibly a lot more powerful.
sentences.zh: 他们是新一代的默多克，而且很可能比后者更强大。

sentences.en: So we're going to talk more about the Ellison's influence and how this deal positions them.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要深入讨论埃里森家族的影响力，以及这笔交易如何定位他们。

sentences.en: But first, I want to talk a little bit about how this deal even came together.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想聊聊这笔交易是如何达成的。

sentences.en: Lauren, the last time you were on the show, you were talking to us about this deal, and it looked at the time like Netflix was going to be the winning bidder, right?
sentences.zh: 劳伦，你上次上节目时谈到这笔交易，当时看起来奈飞似乎会是胜出的竞标者，对吧？

sentences.en: And at the time, Paramount was in the middle of trying to swoop in and outbid them.
sentences.zh: 当时派拉蒙正试图介入并出价超过他们。

sentences.en: So catch us up on what has happened since then.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲后来发生了什么。

sentences.en: So I was on the show shortly after Warner Brothers announced that it had signed a deal with Netflix.
sentences.zh: 我上节目时，华纳兄弟刚宣布与奈飞签署了协议。

sentences.en: Paramount at that point was saying to Warner Brothers board, we think you made a terrible decision.
sentences.zh: 当时派拉蒙对华纳兄弟董事会说：我们认为你们做出了一个糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: And so what they did was they did something called a hostile bid, which they went to Warner Brothers shareholders and said, your board isn't doing right by you.
sentences.zh: 于是他们发起了一项所谓的“敌意收购”，直接向华纳兄弟的股东喊话，称董事会没有维护他们的利益。

sentences.en: We're giving you a better option.
sentences.zh: 我们给你们提供更好的选择。

sentences.en: And it became so loud and so, frankly, compelling that the Warner Brothers board was forced to open a dialogue with Paramount.
sentences.zh: 这种声音变得非常响亮，坦白说也非常有说服力，以至于华纳兄弟董事会被迫与派拉蒙展开对话。

sentences.en: And they said to Netflix, we're going to talk with Paramount and see what they can get.
sentences.zh: 他们对奈飞说：我们要和派拉蒙谈谈，看看他们能提供什么。

sentences.en: Anytime you can come in and offer a higher bid if you want, but we're going to talk to them.
sentences.zh: 你们随时可以提高报价，但我们要先和他们谈谈。

sentences.en: And basically got to the point where the Paramount deal was so good in Warner Brothers' mind,
sentences.zh: 基本上，派拉蒙的方案在华纳兄弟看来非常诱人，

sentences.en: they'd made enough changes that they decided that Paramount's deal was now the better deal.
sentences.zh: 经过多次调整后，他们认为派拉蒙的方案现在是更好的选择。

sentences.en: They're like, not only did they give us everything we wanted, but they threw on a $7 billion fee that they would pay if regulators blocked it.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅满足了我们所有的要求，还额外承诺如果监管机构阻止交易，他们将支付70亿美元的违约金。

sentences.en: So they said, all right, this is better than Netflix.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说：好吧，这比奈飞的方案更好。

sentences.en: Netflix, Paramount's better than you now.
sentences.zh: 奈飞，派拉蒙现在的方案比你们的更好了。

sentences.en: What do you want to do?
sentences.zh: 你们想怎么办？

sentences.en: And Netflix said, actually, we're just going to walk away.
sentences.zh: 奈飞说：那好吧，我们退出。

sentences.en: And now we're here.
sentences.zh: 于是就到了现在这一步。

sentences.en: And Lauren, how much did Paramount agree to buy Warner Brothers for?
sentences.zh: 劳伦，派拉蒙最终同意以多少钱收购华纳兄弟？

sentences.en: Paramount has agreed to buy Warner Brothers for $31 a share.
sentences.zh: 派拉蒙同意以每股31美元的价格收购华纳兄弟。

sentences.en: And just to give a little bit of context, that is 150% premium to the share price of Warner Brothers before any of the M&A talk, which is nearly unheard of in deals.
sentences.zh: 作为背景参考，这比华纳兄弟在任何并购传闻之前的股价溢价了150%，这在交易中几乎是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: And so just to translate a little bit here, I have read that what you just described, Lauren, adds up to a total purchase price of $111 billion.
sentences.zh: 为了翻译一下，我读到过你刚才描述的这些，劳伦，总收购价加起来是1110亿美元。

sentences.en: And a lot of the coverage has basically made it seem like that is way too much to pay.
sentences.zh: 很多报道都认为这个价格高得离谱。

sentences.en: The Paramount has basically overspent on this asset.
sentences.zh: 派拉蒙基本上是在这个资产上花了冤枉钱。

sentences.en: Nicole, can you just explain that a little bit?
sentences.zh: 妮可，你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Like, why is that the criticism?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有这种批评？

sentences.en: Well, last spring, the stock was worth $8 a share.
sentences.zh: 去年春天，该股股价仅为8美元。

sentences.en: And Paramount, when it made its initial bid, offered $19 a share.
sentences.zh: 派拉蒙最初报价时，是每股19美元。

sentences.en: And it went up to $31.
sentences.zh: 后来涨到了31美元。

sentences.en: They also added a $2.8 billion breakup fee to send to Netflix for walking away from the deal.
sentences.zh: 他们还额外支付了28亿美元的违约金给奈飞，作为其退出交易的补偿。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 那可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: The combined company is going to be carrying a debt load that's close to $80 billion, which means they're going to have a lot of debt on their books moving forward.
sentences.zh: 合并后的公司将背负近800亿美元的债务，这意味着他们未来的账面上将有沉重的债务负担。

sentences.en: Yes, they will have 200 million subscribers globally, so they will be in a more effective place to compete against the big streaming services.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们在全球将拥有2亿订阅用户，因此在与大型流媒体服务竞争时，他们将处于更有利的地位。

sentences.en: But it still costs a lot of money to get there.
sentences.zh: 但要达到这一步，成本依然非常高昂。

sentences.en: If we go back to 2019, which was the time when Disney bought Fox for $71 billion, and flash forward to this acquisition, yes, Warner Brothers is bigger than Fox,
sentences.zh: 如果我们回顾2019年，当时迪士尼以710亿美元收购了福克斯，再看看这次收购，没错，华纳兄弟比福克斯更大，

sentences.en: but this is seven years later, and the movie business is not in a healthier state than it was back then pre-COVID.
sentences.zh: 但这是七年之后了，电影行业的状况并不比疫情前更健康。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, this is a business that is facing serious structural challenges.
sentences.zh: 是的，这个行业正面临严峻的结构性挑战。

sentences.en: There's so much competition now for eyeballs, even beyond streaming, just TikTok and social media, and everyone's attention is so fragmented.
sentences.zh: 现在争夺眼球的竞争太激烈了，除了流媒体，还有TikTok和社交媒体，每个人的注意力都被严重碎片化了。

sentences.en: And yeah, the box office numbers are just consistently down every year.
sentences.zh: 而且，票房数据确实每年都在持续下滑。

sentences.en: So just, you know, a couple years ago, even a year ago,
sentences.zh: 所以，就在几年前，甚至一年前，

sentences.en: Warner Brothers' discovery seemed like it was a sinking ship.
sentences.zh: 华纳兄弟探索频道看起来就像一艘正在下沉的船。

sentences.en: I mean, the head of the company, David Zaslav, was kind of doing everything in his power to cut costs, to removing movies from the platform, removing episodes of Sesame Street
sentences.zh: 公司负责人戴维·扎斯拉夫几乎竭尽全力削减成本，从平台上撤下电影，撤下《芝麻街》的剧集，

sentences.en: from the platform so he wouldn't have to pay residuals.
sentences.zh: 这样他就不用支付剩余收益了。

sentences.en: It was like a-
sentences.zh: 这简直是……

sentences.en: Really penny-pinching.
sentences.zh: 真是锱铢必较。

sentences.en: Yes, it was a kind of a desperate situation where he seemed to be basically throwing everything
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种绝望的境地，他似乎要把一切都扔下船，

sentences.en: overboard, and it's just a staggering turnaround over the course of this negotiation.
sentences.zh: 而在这场谈判过程中，情况竟然发生了惊人的逆转。

sentences.en: I mean, hearing you describe all of this, I'm wondering if there's actually a way to think
sentences.zh: 听到你描述这一切，我很好奇，有没有一种可能，

sentences.en: about this as kind of like a huge coup for Netflix, because it sounds like they essentially forced a huge competitor to overpay for one asset and, as you said, also walk away with
sentences.zh: 这其实是奈飞的一场大胜？因为听起来他们本质上是迫使一个巨大的竞争对手为一项资产支付了过高的价格，而且如你所说，还带着28亿美元的违约金全身而退。

sentences.en: a $2.8 billion breakup fee.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们因为没赢得这场竞标战，反而赚了近30亿美元。

sentences.en: So, like, they got paid nearly $3 billion for not winning this bidding war.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们肯定会这样营销，特别是对那些最初对他们参与这笔交易感到非常愤怒的投资者。

sentences.en: Yeah, they are certainly going to market it like that, particularly to their investors who were very mad at them for looking at the deal to begin with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们因为这些举措损失了数十亿美元的市值。

sentences.en: You know, they lost billions on their market cap as part of these efforts.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅从派拉蒙那里拿到了钱，而且还摆脱了一家背负约800亿美元债务的公司。

sentences.en: Not only are they getting money from Paramount to walk away, but they're walking away from a company that's going to have about $80 billion in debt.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森刚才梳理了华纳兄弟面临的许多挑战，其中很大一部分就是债务负担。

sentences.en: Jonathan just walked through a lot of the challenges that Warner Brothers was facing, and a large part of those was its dead load.
sentences.zh: 当你背负巨额债务时，你必须偿还这些债务。

sentences.en: When you have a lot of debt, you have to pay that debt.
sentences.zh: 这使得做其他任何事情的成本都变得更高，你的容错空间也变得更小。

sentences.en: That makes the cost of doing everything else much more expensive, and your margin for error is much more slim.
sentences.zh: 所以，奈飞肯定会告诉市场：我们做出了明智的决定，没有支付过高的价格，并让我们的竞争对手在这一过程中变得伤痕累累，或者陷入困境。

sentences.en: So, Netflix is surely going to tell the market, we made the smart deal in not overpaying and leaving one of our competitors bruised or that kind of in limbo in the process.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，我们现在看到的是派拉蒙收购了一家债台高筑的公司，

sentences.en: So, it sounds like what we have here is Paramount buying a company that is saddled with debt,
sentences.zh: 支付了最高的价格，这反而让奈飞看起来像是在下一盘高明的棋。

sentences.en: paying top dollar, potentially making Netflix look like they're playing 4D chess pretty well, actually.
sentences.zh: 而这一切，我认为引出了一个问题：埃里森家族为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: And all of this, I think, begs the question, why are the Ellisons doing all of this?
sentences.zh: 我们将在休息后深入探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And we're going to get into that after the break.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 我曾在凌晨4点半给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费者产品指南。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最棒的球队。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
53,500 puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: I use a different starting word every day.
25,000 recipes.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 我想聊聊埃里森家族，考虑到这笔交易听起来风险很大。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the Ellisons for a minute, just given how risky this deal sounds.
sentences.zh: 妮可，你认为他们为什么如此渴望达成这笔交易？

sentences.en: Nicole, why do you think they are so desperate for this deal?
sentences.zh: 嗯，戴维·埃里森一直对收购派拉蒙非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: Well, David Ellison was really interested in buying Paramount.
sentences.zh: 他在六个月前完成了那笔交易。

sentences.en: He closed that deal six months ago.
sentences.zh: 但他在那次收购中得到的是一家同样陷入困境的公司，它几年前就开始了自己的流媒体服务，

sentences.en: But what he got in that acquisition was a company that was also struggling, that had started its
sentences.zh: 它有自己的债务负担，有自己的资产库，但这些资产利用率不足，没有得到充分的开发。

sentences.en: own streaming service years ago, that had its own share of debt, that had its own library of assets that were kind of underutilized, that hadn't been exploited as well as they
sentences.zh: 这是一家几经易手、处境并不稳固的公司。

sentences.en: could have been.
sentences.zh: 它在全球拥有近8000万订阅用户。

sentences.en: It was a company that had changed hands over time and was not in a very strong situation.
sentences.zh: 他们还不够大，无法与大型流媒体平台竞争。

sentences.en: It's got close to 80 million subscribers worldwide.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然需要更多资源才能真正成为这个游戏中的玩家。
